text.p: Chevron Corp said on Thursday it has received final approval to modernize its Port Arthur, Texas, cumene production facility.
The project will increase the cumene capacity of the unit from 450 million pounds to one billion pounds per year, Chevron said.
Cumene is used to produce phenol and acetone for the manufacture of products such as building materials, carpets, automotive parts, cosmetics, and medicines.
The engineering design work for the project is being performed by Bechtel Corp, Chevron said.
The project will create approximately 200 construction jobs and is scheduled to begin this month, Chevron said.

The construction contract has been awarded to Halliburton Co's Brown & Root division, Chevron said. The modernization is targeted for completion in September 1997, to coincide with the start-up of a newly expanded ethylene facility, Chevron said.
Project costs were not immediately available.
